rows.title: Sharpness
rows.text: Your eyesight is much blurrier than a human's. In trained bees that had to tell stripes apart, the honeybee, the buff-tailed bumblebee and the common eastern bumblebee each saw about a hundredth as much fine detail as a human. For most other bees and wasps, nobody has measured how sharply they see.
rows.note: Left out hornet, wasp and carpenter bee figures: they come from eye anatomy or partial tables, and the row grade is i.

rows.title: Speed
rows.text: If you are a honeybee, a lamp that looks steady to a human can look like it is flashing to you, because you can see flicker up to about 200 flashes a second, where a human stops at about 60. If you are a bumblebee, you very likely see flicker up to about 130 flashes a second, since that is what was measured in a relative, Bombus hortorum. If you are any other kind of bee or a wasp, nobody has measured how fast you see.
rows.note: Left out the photoreceptor speed records (R2, R3, R5): they give impulse-response half-widths, not a flicker limit, and R5 is a fly.

rows.title: Ultraviolet
rows.text: If you are a honeybee, you have a kind of color-sensing cell for ultraviolet, which is light that humans cannot see at all, and it senses light most strongly at about 345 nanometers. The same cell peaks at about 335 nanometers in the buff-tailed bumblebee and about 345 in the common eastern bumblebee. Nobody has measured how far into the ultraviolet your sensitivity reaches, so only the peak is known.
rows.note: Left out wasps: the record for Dolichovespula norwegica (R14) lists only blue and green cells, so an ultraviolet claim would not fit every species here.

failed.title: Red
failed.last: In the honey bee, three kinds of color-sensing cell have been measured, peaking in ultraviolet, blue and green, and a review reports the same three kinds in the buff-tailed bumblebee, the large red-tailed bumblebee and the European wool carder bee. None of the three kinds peaks in red, even in the large red-tailed bumblebee. If you are another bee, you very likely have these same three kinds.
